docs.title: Welcome to MQSS QIR_Qiskit Documentation
docs.text: QIR_Qiskit is a software tools that translates QIR modules to the Qiskit Quantum Circuits. In this way, the state-of-the-art Qiskit features can be used.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: To get started with the MQSS QIR_Qiskit, please refer to the Getting Started guide.

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text: For information on setting up the development environment and contributing to the project, refer to the Development Guide.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.text:
Detailed API documentation for the MQSS QIR_Qiskit:

  • MQSSQiskitQIRElememts: Desribes the internal representation of the QIR elements
  • MQSSQiskitQIRRegex: The set of auxiliary functions to parse the QIR instructions
  • MQSSQiskitQIRTranslate: The entry point to translate QIR Module to Qiskit Quantum Circuit
  • MQSSQiskitQIRVisitor : The class that helps to iterate over the QIR module

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
This project provides a tool to convert QIR to a Qiskit QuantumCircuit object. The main components of the project are:

  • elements.py: Contains descriptions for the internal representation of the QIR elements.
  • regex.py: Contains a set of auxiliary functions to parse the QIR instructions.
  • translate.py: Contains the entry point to translate QIR Module to Qiskit Quantum Circuit
  • visitor.py: Contains the visitor that helps to iterate over the QIR module

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you start developing, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Python 3.10 to 3.12
  • uv package manager for python

docs.title: Setting Up the Development Environment
docs.text:
Clone the repository:

git clone https://github.com/Munich-Quantum-Software-Stack/QIR-to-Qiskit-Translator
cd QIR2Qiskit

Create a virtual environment and install the dependencies:

uv sync

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
To run the tests, use pytest:

uv run pytest test/test.py

docs.title: Building Documentation
docs.text:
To build the documentation, follow these steps:

Install MkDocs and the Material theme:

uv sync

Build the documentation:

uv run mkdocs build

Local deployment

Run the following and browse the documentation locally at: http://localhost:8000

uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install the MQSS QIR_Qiskit tool, use the following command:

pip install mqss-qir-qiskit

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The QIR_Qiskit allows users to translate QIR Modules to the state-of-the-art Qiskit Quantum Circuits. In this way, user can use Qiskit feature as well. The main components are:

  • MQSSQiskitQIRElememts: Desribes the internal representation of the QIR elements
  • MQSSQiskitQIRRegex: The set of auxiliary functions to parse the QIR instructions
  • MQSSQiskitQIRTranslate: The entry point to translate QIR Module to Qiskit Quantum Circuit
  • MQSSQiskitQIRVisitor : The class that helps to iterate over the QIR module

docs.title: Import Required Modules
docs.text:
Import the necessary component from MQSS QIR_Qiskit package and auxiliary component from pathlib.

from mqss.qir_qiskit import to_qiskit_circuit

from pathlib import Path

docs.title: Import the Bitcode
docs.text:
Import the bitcode as bytes from the file

bitcode = Path(bitcode_path).read_bytes()

docs.title: Translate the Bitcode
docs.text:
Translate the Bitcode to the Qiskit Quantum Circuit

quantum_circuit = to_qiskit_circuit(bitcode)

docs.title: Use Human-Readable QIR
docs.text:
To translate Human-Readable QIR to the Qiskit Quantum Circuit, first we need to create Module to extract bitcode, then we can translate to Qiskit Quantum Circuit.

from pyqir import (
    Context,
    Module,
)

qir = Path(human_readable_qir_path).read_text()
module = Module.from_ir(Context(), qir)
bitcode = module.bitcode
quantum_circuit = to_qiskit_circuit(bitcode)
